topic.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Objectives and Policy Improvement
topic.overview: Deep reinforcement learning uses neural representations to estimate values or choose actions from experience. This topic studies policy improvement, value architectures, gradient estimation, differentiable simulation, and objectives that adapt during training. The shared challenge is using limited interactions efficiently when targets and data distributions change as the agent learns.
topic.whyItMatters: Algorithmic components interact: a better value representation may change exploration, while off-policy data can improve reuse but complicate learning. Simulation and adaptive objectives offer additional information, yet their benefits must be tested against the assumptions they introduce and the reliability of the resulting behavior.
topic.evolution: A 1996 method improves an existing controller through Monte Carlo action evaluation. Deep value and policy-gradient methods dominate later representatives. In 2020, meta-gradients learn an objective online from interaction, addressing bootstrapping and nonstationarity. Recent work examines residual value learning and flow-based temporal-difference methods, alongside security studies exposing vulnerabilities in trained agents.
openQuestions: When can learned objectives adapt safely to changing environments?
Which gains in interaction efficiency persist when simulators or replay data are imperfect?
